DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra.summary: Mathlib already supplies much of the classical background this roadmap plans: continuous maps out of power-series rings with uniqueness, the universal property of an adically complete ring as the limit of its quotients by powers of the maximal ideal (with those powers cofinal among Artinian quotients), regular sequences, projective dimension and the Rees theorem, the dimension formula along flat maps, fibre products of local rings, Weierstrass division, topological Nakayama for complete modules, and for complexes the theorem that quasi-isomorphisms between bounded-above projective complexes are homotopy equivalences, the canonical t-structure and spectral sequences of spectral objects; Tau Ceti adds Koszul-signed symmetric monoidal complexes of modules, an Euler–Poincaré theorem for additive invariants, minimal projective presentations and dual-number tangent vectors. Genuinely missing are the roadmap's own objects: depth as an invariant, Cohen–Macaulay and complete-intersection rings, Auslander–Buchsbaum, catenary and excellent rings, completed tensor products and Noetherianity of completions, small extensions, Schlessinger's criterion and deformation functors, perfect complexes, Tor-amplitude, derived tensor products, derived completion and lim¹, and all of patching, ultrapatching and component-support theory. P7, R03.1 and R03.3 are partly built; the other six layers are not built.

targets.target: Homotopy-equivalence and quasi-isomorphism API for bounded complexes of finite projective modules
targets.note: Mathlib proves, in any abelian category, that a cochain complex of projectives which is bounded above is K-projective, and that a morphism between K-projective complexes is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when it is a homotopy equivalence (with the ℕ-indexed chain-complex form). ModuleCat over a complete Noetherian local O-algebra is a special case (the derived category is available through the `HasDerivedCategory.standard` construction, not an instance), so this API should be consumed; only finiteness bookkeeping is specific to the layer.

targets.target: Perfect complexes, defined through local finite projective resolutions
targets.note: No perfect complex, `Perf` subcategory or pseudo-coherence notion exists in either tree; 'perfect complex' occurs in no Lean file of Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

targets.target: Minimal representatives over a local ring and their uniqueness up to homotopy
targets.note: Only two-term pieces exist: Tau Ceti's minimal projective presentations P₁ → P₀ → M → 0 (projective cover plus superfluous kernel, image in the radical, unique up to isomorphism; existence over semiprimary rings), and Mathlib's freeness of finite flat modules over a local ring and the minimal number of generators as the dimension modulo m. Minimal complexes of arbitrary length over a local ring, and uniqueness of minimal representatives up to homotopy, are absent.

targets.target: Tor-amplitude, kept distinct from the amplitude of a chosen complex and from the degrees of nonzero cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib has the canonical t-structure on the derived category, with `IsLE`/`IsGE` characterised by vanishing of cohomology (the degrees of nonzero cohomology), and shows an object with cohomology in [a,b] is represented by a complex strictly concentrated in [a,b] (the amplitude of a chosen complex). Tor-amplitude, flat dimension and Tor dimension are absent from both trees.

targets.target: Duals of complexes and the derived tensor product
targets.note: Mathlib has the tensor product of homological complexes and Tor as left-derived functors of the tensor product; Tau Ceti makes cochain complexes of R-modules a symmetric monoidal category with the Koszul sign and builds the R-linear Hom complex. There is no derived tensor product or RHom on the derived category, and no duality theory for perfect complexes.

targets.target: Derived completion, derived Nakayama and specialisation/extension under derived completeness and finiteness
targets.note: Neither library has derived completeness or a derived Nakayama lemma; Mathlib's Nakayama lemmas are for modules only.

targets.target: Spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^{j−i}(C⊗ᴸ_A B) and its convergence
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the spectral sequence of a spectral object in an abelian category (with first- and third-quadrant E₂ versions) and the spectral object attached to a filtered complex in the homotopy category. No Tor or base-change spectral sequence is constructed, and the derived tensor product it abuts to is missing.

targets.target: Finite coefficient quotients before inverse limits: derived Mittag-Leffler comparisons and a retained lim¹
targets.note: Mathlib's Mittag-Leffler condition is stated for cofiltered systems of types (eventual ranges); an ℕ-indexed system with surjective transition maps has a limit mapping onto each stage; adic completion of finite modules over a Noetherian ring is exact. There is no lim¹, derived inverse limit or Milnor sequence, and no Mittag-Leffler theory for systems of modules or complexes.

targets.target: Morphisms, homotopies and Hecke actions compatible through the inverse system at chain level
targets.note: Nothing in either library about compatible chain-level actions on inverse systems of complexes.

duplicates.note: Hecke actions on bounded perfect complexes, comparing chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions over complete coefficient rings: the chain-versus-cohomology distinction of P7's last paragraph.
Owns generic derived completion (Koszul model, conservativity of reduction) and tracks lim¹ and Tor terms; P7's derived completion and derived Nakayama are its affine local case.
Defines perfectness locally by bounded finite locally free complexes and compares affine perfect complexes with perfect modules over the coordinate ring.
Constructs the derived inverse limit and Milnor sequence, keeps lim¹ instead of commuting completion with cohomology, and asks for Hecke-action compatibility along the tower.
Proves the Mittag-Leffler and lim¹ statements before interchanging cohomology with inverse limits of finite coefficient quotients.
Bounded complexes of finite projective modules with quasi-isomorphism, duals and derived base change, plus Mittag-Leffler arguments for compact inverse systems.

targets.target: Patching data (R_N, S_N, C_N): S_N a finite quotient of O[Δ_N] with bounded generator rank, C_N with uniformly bounded finite projective presentations, and compatible augmentations, residual rings, framings and transition maps
targets.note: Group rings and their augmentation (with its kernel spanned by the g − 1, in Tau Ceti) exist; nothing presents O[Δ_N] as a quotient of a power-series ring and no patching datum of this kind appears in either tree.

targets.target: Ultrapatching with a fixed ultrafilter; independence of representatives and comparison of presentations and transition maps
targets.note: Mathlib has ultrafilters, germs of maps into a fixed ring or module along a filter (ultrapowers) and Łoś's theorem for first-order ultraproducts. `Filter.Product` of a varying family carries no algebraic structure, so there is no ultraproduct of varying rings and modules, and nothing about ultrapatching or its independence statements.

targets.target: Uniform bounds, compactness of finite presentation data and cofinality before passing to the limit
targets.note: The abstract compactness step is in Mathlib: a cofiltered (or inverse) system of nonempty finite types has a section, a form of König's lemma. Its application to bounded presentation data of patching systems is absent.

targets.target: S_∞ = O[[z₁,…,z_q]], the patched deformation base R_∞ and its continuous action on C_∞ in the derived category
targets.note: O[[z₁,…,z_q]] exists as `MvPowerSeries`, is Noetherian for finitely many variables, adically complete (an instance in `AdicCompletion/Completeness.lean`) and has the continuous universal property. R_∞, C_∞ and the action are absent.

targets.target: Augmentation isomorphism C_∞⊗ᴸ_{S_∞}O ≅ C_original, finite generation and perfectness of C_∞, comparison of finite-level Hecke actions
targets.note: Depends on patched objects, derived tensor products and perfect complexes, none of which exists.

duplicates.note: Fixes a nonprincipal ultrafilter as in ACC+ §6.4.1 and proves the arithmetic tower satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching, assigning the abstract construction to this layer.
Applies the abstract patching construction to the actual rings and modules, with presentation, depth and framing-variable bookkeeping.
Constructs a patched completed module with finite generation, projectivity and support assertions.

targets.target: Inequalities relating codimension of support, projective dimension and Tor-amplitude over a regular local base
targets.note: Mathlib has support dimension, projective dimension and their behaviour under regular sequences over a Noetherian local ring, and regular local rings. The inequalities themselves (new intersection theorem type) and Tor-amplitude are absent.

targets.target: Balanced-dimension conclusions of Calegari–Geraghty, including non-Cohen–Macaulay and torsion cases via support of the whole perfect complex
targets.note: No Cohen–Macaulay predicate, perfect complexes or support of a complex in either tree.

targets.target: One-degree module theorem as a specialisation; integral support versus support after inverting p
targets.note: Mathlib relates module support to localisation (M[1/f] = 0 iff Supp M ⊆ V(f)) and to quotients (Supp(M/IM) = Supp M ∩ V(I) for finite M). There is no support of a complex, no one-degree concentration theorem and no statement separating integral support from support after inverting p for complexes.

targets.target: Component-support transport under finite flat coefficient change, removal of framing variables, specialisation of local conditions and comparison of two patched systems
targets.note: Nothing about framing variables, components of patched supports or their transport.

targets.target: Nearly faithful, radical-annihilator and union-of-components conclusions
targets.note: Annihilators, radicals and minimal primes exist; 'nearly faithful' and theorems of this shape do not.

targets.target: Algebraic derived Ihara-avoidance lemmas comparing support when auxiliary local types change
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Derived length identity of ACC+ §6.3.4: idempotent localisation of a derived T-action on a perfect S-complex over an excellent base, dimension-zero vanishing and dimension-one generic-length formula for the Euler characteristic mod f
targets.note: Ingredients exist: additivity of length and length along flat local extensions (Mathlib); in Tau Ceti, the Euler–Poincaré identity for any additive invariant on a strictly bounded complex, length(I/aI) = ord(a), and the decomposition of a module by a complete family of orthogonal idempotents. Derived actions of a finite algebra in D(S), their idempotent localisation, the length-valued Euler characteristic of a perfect complex modulo f, the generic-length formula and excellent rings are absent.

duplicates.note: Compares patched complexes for two systems of local conditions: component support, characteristic-zero localisation, near faithfulness and the derived Ihara-avoidance support implication.
Local component matching and patched support, with the same warning that a Cohen–Macaulay patched module on one component says nothing about another.
Support and multiplicity assertions for patched completed modules, not inferred from dense sets of points.
Same roadmap: the module-level statement of support transport, faithfulness, near faithfulness and union-of-components conclusions.

targets.target: The coefficient categories: Artinian local O-algebras with residue field k, and complete Noetherian local O-algebras with local continuous morphisms
targets.note: Every ingredient predicate exists, but neither library bundles them into a category with a fixed residue-field identification.

targets.target: Presentation of a complete local ring as the inverse limit of its Artinian quotients
targets.note: Mathlib proves the ingredients: an I-adically complete ring is its completion, with the universal property that compatible maps into all R/I^n lift uniquely (`IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom`, `eq_liftRingHom`); every Artinian quotient of a local ring contains a power of the maximal ideal, so the powers are cofinal; and R/I is Artinian when m is minimal over I in a Noetherian local ring. The single statement 'R is the limit of its Artinian quotients' in a coefficient category is not packaged.

targets.target: Continuous homomorphisms out of power-series rings into complete local rings, with uniqueness
targets.note: For a complete Hausdorff linearly topologised target S, a continuous coefficient map and elements that are topologically nilpotent and tend to zero, `eval₂Hom` is the continuous ring map out of `MvPowerSeries σ R`, and `eval₂_unique`/`aeval_unique` give uniqueness among continuous maps. A complete Noetherian local O-algebra with its m-adic topology satisfies these hypotheses.

targets.target: Completed tensor products over O, with the exact conditions under which they stay Noetherian and local
targets.note: No completed tensor product A ⊗̂_O B exists. Mathlib compares completion of a finite module with base change along the completed Noetherian ring and proves the completion of a local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal is local and complete; it has no theorem that the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian (Tau Ceti has this only for strongly Noetherian Huber rings).

targets.target: Residue-field extension of the coefficient ring
targets.note: Residue fields, their functoriality and invariance under completion exist; W(k) is a p-adically complete DVR for a perfect field k of characteristic p; a finite étale extension of local rings has rank equal to its residue degree. The change of coefficients O → O' realising a given residue-field extension (the unramified extension of a complete DVR) is not constructed.

targets.target: Descent and ascent of finite generation along these maps
targets.note: The engine of topological Nakayama is in Mathlib: for M I-adically precomplete and N I-adically Hausdorff, a linear map that is surjective modulo I is surjective (no finiteness assumed). Also: finiteness modulo a finitely generated nilpotent kernel lifts, the span criterion modulo m for finite modules over a local ring, and transitivity. The statements in the layer's form (a complete local O-algebra, or a complete separated module, that is finite modulo the maximal ideal is finite) are not stated.

targets.target: APIs for nilpotent ideals, small extensions and square-zero extensions
targets.note: Mathlib has induction from nilpotent to square-zero ideals, the trivial square-zero extension, the bijection between lifts across a square-zero ideal and derivations, extensions of algebras and formally smooth lifting along square-zero ideals. Small extensions of Artinian local rings (surjections with principal kernel killed by the maximal ideal) are absent.

duplicates.note: Constructs completed tensor products with their topology and universal property (for Huber pairs), the construction R03.1 needs over O.
Topological Nakayama and finite generation from a finite residual quotient, the complete-local finite-generation statements of R03.1.
Relates local deformation rings over O to residue-field extension of the coefficients.
Works over the same base category of Artinian local W(k)-algebras with residue field k.

targets.target: Schlessinger's criterion in the form used for unframed deformation functors
targets.note: No functors on Artinian local algebras and no representability criterion in either tree; 'Schlessinger' occurs nowhere.

targets.target: Framed representability construction
targets.note: No deformation functors or deformation rings exist in either library.

targets.target: Tangent-space finiteness
targets.note: The representable case is present in pieces: the cotangent space m/m² of a local ring with dimension equal to the minimal number of generators of m (finite-dimensional for Noetherian rings), Tau Ceti's identification of dual-number points over a given point with derivations, and finiteness of the cotangent space of an augmented algebra. The tangent space F(k[ε]) of a general deformation functor and its finiteness are absent.

targets.target: Fibre products of Artinian local rings and the Schlessinger conditions on F(A×_C B) → F(A)×_{F(C)}F(B)
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the fibre product of ring and algebra maps and proves it is local when one factor is local and the other map is a local homomorphism. It does not prove the fibre product of Artinian rings is Artinian, and the Schlessinger conditions are absent.

targets.target: Hulls versus prorepresenting objects, and uniqueness of hulls
targets.note: No hulls, versal or prorepresentable functors on Artinian algebras (Mathlib's 'prorepresentability' concerns Galois categories).

targets.target: Presentation relations related to obstruction spaces
targets.note: Mathlib has the naive cotangent complex of a presentation, its first homology and the Jacobi–Zariski sequence, which measure the relations of a presentation, but no obstruction theory for deformation functors and no bound on relations by an obstruction space.

duplicates.note: Existence of universal framed rings and of unframed rings under absolute irreducibility, and the framed/unframed comparison by power-series maps.
Tangent and obstruction descriptions and the bound on the number of relations of a global presentation (KW II Prop. 4.5, Cor. 4.7).
Framed local representability with its tangent/obstruction description.
Pro-representability on Artinian local W(k)-algebras with residue field k, and a parameter criterion for generators of the maximal ideal of the prorepresenting ring.

targets.target: Regular sequences
targets.note: Weakly regular and regular sequences on modules over a commutative ring, with permutation, quotient, localisation and flat base-change lemmas.

targets.target: Depth
targets.note: Mathlib proves Rees' theorem (Noetherian R, finite M with IM ≠ M: an M-regular sequence of length n in I exists iff Ext^i(R/I, M) = 0 for i < n) but defines no depth invariant; `RegularSequence.lean` lists depth as a TODO.

targets.target: Cohen–Macaulay rings and modules
targets.note: No Cohen–Macaulay (or maximal Cohen–Macaulay, Gorenstein local) predicate in either tree.

targets.target: Projective dimension
targets.note: Projective dimension in abelian categories, with pd(M/xM) = pd(M)+1 for M-regular x in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring and pd_R(R/(x₁,…,x_n)) = n for a regular sequence (stated for `ModuleCat.{v} R` with `[Small.{v} R]`).

targets.target: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula
targets.note: Absent; 'Auslander' occurs only in Tau Ceti's Auslander–Reiten theory for Artin algebras.

targets.target: Complete-intersection criteria used in patching
targets.note: No complete-intersection predicate for local rings in either tree.

targets.target: Depth and dimension formulas under the local maps used
targets.note: The dimension half is largely present: ht(P) = ht(p) + ht(P/pS) under going-down (Matsumura 13.B Th. 19), and flat algebras have going-down, which gives dim B = dim A + dim B/m_A B for flat local maps; quotienting by a regular sequence drops dimension by its length. For power series only dim R + 1 ≤ dim R[[X]] is proved (`ringKrullDim_succ_le_ringKrullDim_powerseries`), and no depth formula exists.

targets.target: Equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules
targets.note: Associated primes (finitely many for finite modules over Noetherian rings), support, support dimension and the bijection between minimal primes and irreducible components of Spec are in Mathlib; equidimensionality is not defined.

targets.target: Catenarity and excellence as explicit hypotheses
targets.note: No catenary or excellent ring predicate in either tree; a Tau Ceti docstring records the absence of `IsExcellent`.

duplicates.note: Owns regularity and dimension under completion of Noetherian local rings and miracle flatness for finite maps of regular local schemes, dimension and depth statements along the local maps R03.3 also needs.
States maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules over a hypersurface S/(w) (Eisenbud), so it needs the same Cohen–Macaulay theory.

targets.target: A characteristic-zero point of a finite O-algebra from a dimension or non-torsion hypothesis
targets.note: No statement producing an O-algebra map to the integers of a finite extension of Frac(O) from non-torsion or positive dimension in either library; Mathlib has only the lying-over of minimal primes and an algebraic closure of ℚ_p.

targets.target: Finite-over-a-subring criteria of KW II §10 and their completed versions
targets.note: Mathlib has Weierstrass division and preparation over a complete local ring (the one-variable engine of such criteria) and the integral-plus-finite-type criterion for finiteness. The criteria of KW II §10 and their completed versions (finiteness over a power-series subring detected modulo its maximal ideal) are not stated.

targets.target: A finite unframed global deformation ring kept separate from its framed power-series enlargement
targets.note: Depends on deformation rings, which neither library has.

duplicates.note: Obtains a point over a finite extension of the coefficient field with nonzero characteristic, stressing that finiteness and nonzeroness alone are insufficient.
KW II Theorem 10.1 finiteness of the unframed global ring, noting that the framed power-series enlargement is not finite over O.

targets.target: Inverse-limit patching of finite-level rings, modules, presentations and transition data, with the compactness or diagonal-subsequence argument
targets.note: No patching construction in either tree. The abstract compactness principle (sections of a cofiltered system of nonempty finite sets) is in Mathlib.

targets.target: Existence and finite generation of the patched module and its power-series action
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Specialisation of the patched module and the depth comparison
targets.note: Absent; the depth comparison also lacks a depth invariant.

targets.target: Integral assertions kept separate from those after inverting π
targets.note: Localisation away from an element is standard, but none of the patching statements exist in either form.

targets.target: The abstract patching theorem with all numerical hypotheses and the faithfulness/support conclusion actually obtained
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Same roadmap: the complex-level version of this inverse-limit patching, with uniform bounds, cofinality and specialisation.
Applies the abstract patching construction to the actual rings and modules, proving each presentation and depth hypothesis.
Proves the arithmetic tower satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses consumed by the abstract patching theorem.
Constructs a patched completed module with finite generation and support assertions.

targets.target: Support transport along flat maps, coefficient changes, quotient maps and removal of framing variables
targets.note: Mathlib has the inclusion of the support over an algebra in the preimage of the support over the base, Supp(M/IM) = Supp M ∩ V(I) for finite M, vanishing after inverting f in terms of support, and monotonicity under surjections. The base-change formula Supp(B ⊗_A M) = preimage of Supp M along flat or finite maps, and anything about framing variables, are absent.

targets.target: When a patched module is faithful, nearly faithful or supported on a specified union of components
targets.note: Faithfulness as vanishing of the annihilator and minimal primes as irreducible components exist; near faithfulness and the patched support-on-components criteria do not.

targets.target: An explicit algebraic theorem for the torsion-free/reduced quotient at which R=T concludes, and a stronger theorem under extra hypotheses
targets.note: Radicals and the reduced quotient by a radical ideal exist; the R=T conclusions are absent.

duplicates.note: Same roadmap: the complex-level component-support transport, near faithfulness and union-of-components conclusions.
Keeps equality of reduced supports, equality after inverting p, near faithfulness and integral R=T distinct when comparing patched systems.
States when the generic-fibre or integral R=T statement strengthens, the arithmetic form of R03.6's last target.
Support and multiplicity assertions for patched modules.

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions.summary: Neither library has a Habiro ring, a cyclotomic completion, q-Pochhammer symbols or any of Habiro's rigidity theorems, so every mathematical layer is not built and HC.6 is process. The supporting theory is extensive and should be consumed: Mathlib's cyclotomic arithmetic (q^n − 1 = ∏_{d|n}Φ_d, Φ_n(1), norms of ζ − 1, factor counts of Φ_n over finite fields, q ↦ q^p expansions), resultants with Bézout identities, division by monic polynomials, Taylor expansion with Hasse derivatives and the factorial comparison, power-series substitution under topological nilpotence, ideal-filter topologies, separated completions with their universal property, the Chinese remainder theorem and idempotent decompositions; Tau Ceti adds uniqueness for maps out of completions, equality of topologies from mutually cofinal bases, limits of complete separated topological rings, kernels of completion maps, and executable arithmetic modulo monic and cyclotomic polynomials. What is genuinely missing is the completion R[q]^S itself and everything built on it: factorial expansions and algorithms, evaluation and Taylor maps on the completion, adjacency and Habiro's Theorems 4.1, 5.2 and 6.1, and completed modules with their component decompositions.

targets.target: The multiplicative monoid generated by Φ_n(q), n ∈ S, ordered by divisibility, and its directedness
targets.note: Cyclotomic polynomials over any ring (monic, defined by base change from ℤ) and generated submonoids exist; the directed monoid used as an index set is not constructed.

targets.target: R[q]^S as the inverse limit of the quotients R[q]/(f), with projections, compatible quotient maps, independence of representatives and the dense polynomial map
targets.note: The generic constructions exist: the linear topology on a ring defined by a filter of ideals, its separated completion, limits of commutative rings, and (Tau Ceti) all small limits of complete Hausdorff topological commutative rings. R[q]^S itself, its projections and its identification of the completion with lim R[q]/(f) are not constructed; nothing named Habiro exists in either tree.

targets.target: Completeness, separatedness, extensionality by finite quotients and the universal property for continuous maps to complete separated rings
targets.note: The universal property of the separated completion of a topological ring (existence, and uniqueness in Tau Ceti) and the adic-complete lifting property exist in general; they are not specialised to R[q]^S or to its finite quotients.

targets.target: Injectivity of R[q] → R[q]^S only under hypotheses on R and S
targets.note: Tau Ceti identifies the kernel of A → Â with the closure of 0, the general tool for such injectivity statements; the cyclotomic-completion statements and their hypotheses are absent.

targets.target: For S = ℕ_{>0}: cofinality of P_N(q) = ∏_{i≤N}(1−q^i), identification with lim_N R[q]/(P_N) and with the (q^m−1)-completions, counting cyclotomic multiplicities
targets.note: q^n − 1 = ∏_{d|n} Φ_d over any ring (the input for the multiplicity count), equality of topologies from mutually cofinal submodule bases (Tau Ceti) and lifting from a cofinal subsequence of powers in the adic case exist. P_N(q) has no carrier (Mathlib lists q-Pochhammer symbols as a TODO) and the cofinality and limit comparisons are absent.

targets.target: Continuous functoriality in R, contravariant restriction in S, identity and composition laws, equivalences for cofinal systems, and completed versus uncompleted base change
targets.note: Functoriality of completion, the cofinal-bases principle and the Noetherian finite comparison of adic completion with base change exist; the statements for cyclotomic completions do not.

duplicates.note: States the limit description by (q^m−1)-completions indexed by divisibility and the cofinal Habiro-factorial tower, for its derived completion.
Proves that the divisor system and a cofinal factorial sequence give canonically equivalent limits, the relative form of HC.1's cofinality comparison.
Compares the number-field Habiro ring with the usual Habiro completion when F = ℚ and Δ = 1, so it restates the classical completion.

targets.target: Representatives successively modulo P_N and a convergent factorial expansion ∑ a_N(q)P_N(q) of every compatible element
targets.note: No factorial expansion exists; only the general convergence criterion in complete nonarchimedean groups (multiplicative form cited; the additive form is generated from it).

targets.target: Normalised degree-bounded expansion by division by monic polynomials, with existence and uniqueness
targets.note: Division with remainder by a monic polynomial over any commutative ring, with the degree bound and uniqueness, is in Mathlib and each P_N is monic; the normalised expansion built from it is not stated.

targets.target: Addition, multiplication and coefficient-extraction algorithms on normalised expansions, each with a congruence correctness theorem and finite-precision dependence
targets.note: Tau Ceti has executable, proved-correct arithmetic modulo a monic polynomial (synthetic division on coefficient lists) and exact ℤ[q]/(Φ_e) arithmetic; algorithms on factorial expansions of Habiro-ring elements are absent.

targets.target: q is invertible in the Habiro ring, its inverse at finite precision, and the comparison of polynomial and Laurent-polynomial constructions
targets.note: Generic unit criteria (a^n = 1 ⇒ a unit; 1 + Jacobson radical consists of units) and Laurent polynomials as the localisation at X exist; the statements for the Habiro ring are absent.

duplicates.note: Also proves q invertible in the completed coefficient ring and warns against confusing completion with inverting q^m − 1.
Builds finite truncations of cyclotomic (q;q)_n expansions and proves coefficient compatibility before passing to the completion.

targets.target: Evaluation at a root ζ of order d ∈ S into R[ζ] through a finite quotient, independent of the truncation
targets.note: R[q]/(Φ_d) as `AdjoinRoot`, Φ_d as the minimal polynomial of a primitive root over ℤ, and Tau Ceti's exact ℤ[ζ_e] identified with `AdjoinRoot Φ_e` exist; evaluation out of the completion does not.

targets.target: The Taylor map into R[ζ][[q−ζ]] from compatible quotient maps, with constant term the evaluation
targets.note: For polynomials Mathlib has f ↦ f(X + r) as an algebra automorphism whose constant coefficient is f(r); the Taylor map of the completed ring into power series in q − ζ is absent.

targets.target: Higher Taylor coefficients identified with Hasse derivatives, keeping factorial denominators when comparing with ordinary derivatives
targets.note: At polynomial level this is exactly Mathlib: coefficient n of `taylor r f` is (hasseDeriv n f)(r), and n!·hasseDeriv n is the n-th derivative. It should be consumed; only the passage to finite quotients and the completion is missing.

targets.target: Naturality under coefficient change, root conjugation, order restriction and q ↦ q^a
targets.note: Coefficient change for Hasse derivatives and cyclotomic polynomials and the substitution q ↦ q^p on cyclotomic polynomials exist at polynomial level; completed versions do not.

targets.target: p-adic re-expansion maps, defined through topological nilpotence in a complete coefficient ring, with their cocycle law
targets.note: Mathlib's substitution into power series requires exactly the nilpotence hypothesis the layer insists on and proves composition of substitutions; the specific re-expansions and their cocycle identity are absent.

duplicates.note: Proves substitution by ζ_{pm} − ζ_m exists in the required completion and defines the Frobenius-twisted Taylor-gluing condition.
Root-of-unity choices, change-of-choice invariance and convergence of the p-adic substitutions in the Taylor presentation of the relative ring.
Takes the Taylor expansion at q = 1 (the Ohtsuki series) and root-of-unity evaluations of one completed element.

targets.target: Adjacency of cyclotomic orders through prime-power ratios, and p-adic separatedness of R
targets.note: The arithmetic behind adjacency is proved: Φ_{p^k}(1) = p and Φ_n(1) = 1 otherwise, and N(ζ_n − 1) is p for prime powers and 1 otherwise; p-adic separatedness is `IsHausdorff (span {p})`. The adjacency relation is not defined.

targets.target: Cyclotomic resultant and comaximality lemmas
targets.note: General resultants with the Bézout identity and 'unit resultant iff coprime', and coprimality of distinct Φ_n over ℚ, exist; Res(Φ_m, Φ_n) and comaximality of cyclotomic ideals in ℤ[q] or R[q] are absent.

targets.target: Habiro Theorem 4.1: a connected chain of orders gives injective restriction, with the full chain hypothesis
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Habiro Theorem 5.2: rootwise Taylor injectivity under the coefficient-domain and separation hypotheses
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: For ℤ and all positive orders, a single Taylor expansion determines the completed element
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Habiro Theorem 6.1 (evaluation uniqueness with the infinite-set condition) and the non-surjectivity examples of §7.4
targets.note: Absent.

HabiroRings.summary: Nothing specific to this roadmap exists: neither library has λ- or Λ-rings, Adams operations, q-Witt vectors, derived completion, E∞-algebras, spectra, solid tensor products, algebraic K-theory above K₀ or any Habiro ring, so HR.1–HR.6 are not built and HR.7 is process. The general tools it consumes are present in Mathlib: formally étale lifting along square-zero ideals, lifting into adically complete rings and uniqueness under ⋂ Iⁱ = 0 (the mechanism for the Frobenius lift on completed étale algebras), p-typical Witt vectors with ghost maps, Frobenius and Verschiebung, cyclotomic arithmetic including Φ_{p^k m} = Φ_m^{φ(p^k)} in characteristic p, equalizers with flat base change, invertible modules and Picard groups. The roadmap's warning that Φ_m need not stay irreducible modulo ℓ is already a Mathlib theorem: Φ_m has φ(m)/ord_m(q) factors over a finite field of order q, so Φ₅ over 𝔽₁₁ has four linear factors. The concrete equalizer universal property of Suggested.lean is also already in Mathlib.

ComputationalNumberTheory.summary: The libraries already have the exact small-scale arithmetic this roadmap assumes and several certified results it would otherwise rebuild: executable ℤ, ℚ and ZMod, Lucas' primality theorem, Fermat pseudoprimes, Carmichael numbers, Lucas–Lehmer and Pépin tests, certified factorisation of numerals, Kummer–Dedekind for primes prime to the index, the unit-index formula, the Minkowski bound, and Sturm bounds (Mathlib at level one, Tau Ceti for all finite-index subgroups); Tau Ceti adds exact computable cyclotomic integers, the index-discriminant formula, worked class numbers, Hecke coefficient formulas, point counts and 2-descent. Genuinely missing are the algorithms and their certificates: Pratt certificates, Miller–Rabin and AKS, polynomial factorisation over finite fields, Hermite normal form and LLL, Round 2, general class-group and unit computations, modular symbols, Schoof and Vélu, interval or ball arithmetic, root isolation, L-value enclosures, cost models, and database certificate schemas. CN.0, CN.1 and CN.3 are partly built, CN.2 and CN.4 not built, and CN.5 is process; CN.2 still lists the retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4 as an input.

targets.target: Exact integers, rationals and residue rings ℤ/n with executable arithmetic and decidable equality
targets.note: ℤ, ℚ and ZMod n are exact, computable carriers with Mathlib's ring structures and decidable equality; binary numerals for kernel computation (`PosNum`, `Num`) also exist.

targets.target: Finite fields with computable presentations and conversions to the canonical carrier
targets.note: Prime fields ZMod p are executable, but `GaloisField p n` is defined abstractly as a splitting field and is not executable; no computable presentation F_p[X]/(f) with a proved isomorphism to it exists.

targets.target: Exact algebraic numbers with computable presentations whose conversions carry equality and embedding proofs
targets.note: Tau Ceti has exactly this pattern for cyclotomic integers: an executable coefficient-list model of ℤ[ζ_e] identified with `AdjoinRoot Φ_e` (with a pinned complex embedding) and kernel-computable coefficients of Φ_n proved equal to Mathlib's. General algebraic numbers (isolating intervals, minimal polynomials) have no computable presentation.

targets.target: Ideals and lattices with computable presentations (Hermite/Smith normal forms, reduced bases)
targets.note: Lattices and the existence of Smith normal forms (Mathlib over a PID; Tau Ceti for integer matrices with uniqueness) are present, and Tau Ceti has a proved-correct computable Gauss–Jordan elimination over fields. There is no Hermite normal form, no HNF representation of ideals and no LLL.

targets.target: p-adic approximations with explicit precision
targets.note: Truncation of p-adic integers modulo pⁿ with its specification exists; a precision-tracking representation of p-adic numbers with operations and conversion proofs does not.

targets.target: Bit-complexity, randomness and precision models, with success and error guarantees for randomised algorithms
targets.note: Mathlib has time-bounded and polynomial-time computability for multi-stack Turing machines and the probability-mass-function monad. The RAM cost model of Shoup §3.2 that the decomposition fixes, bit-complexity statements for arithmetic, and error guarantees for randomised algorithms are absent.

duplicates.note: Smith and Hermite normal forms with certified change-of-basis matrices and effective ideal arithmetic, the lattice and ideal presentations CN.0 specifies.
Certified LLL-style lattice reduction with exact change-of-basis certificates.
Certified algebraic numbers with isolating intervals and local precision on exact carriers; it imports CN.0's presentations and restates their certificate discipline.

targets.target: Primality certificates (Lucas/Pratt) with an independent checker
targets.note: Lucas' theorem, the basis of Pratt certificates, is proved with its converse, and `norm_num` proves `Nat.Prime n` by a checked trial-division certificate (practical only for small n). A Pratt certificate structure and checker is an explicit TODO in `LucasPrimality.lean`.

targets.target: Source-scoped probabilistic tests (Fermat, Miller–Rabin with |L'_n| ≤ (n−1)/4) and the Carmichael obstruction, with probable prime and proven prime as separate notions
targets.note: Fermat probable primes and pseudoprimes (a notion separate from `Nat.Prime`), Carmichael numbers and Korselt's criterion are in Mathlib. Strong pseudoprimes, the Miller–Rabin sets L_n and L'_n with their bounds, Solovay–Strassen and randomised error bounds are absent.

targets.target: Source-scoped deterministic tests (AKS, and special-form tests)
targets.note: Deterministic tests for special forms exist: Lucas–Lehmer for Mersenne numbers (both directions, with a `norm_num` extension) and Pépin's test for Fermat numbers. AKS — the characterisation of primes by (X+a)ⁿ = Xⁿ + a, the algorithm, its correctness and its running time — is absent; only the characteristic-p binomial identity exists.

targets.target: Integer factorisation with checked factors (the product of the output is the input and every factor is prime)
targets.note: Mathlib's `Nat.primeFactorsList` multiplies back to n, and the simproc `Nat.primeFactorsList_ofNat` (`Tactic/Simproc/Factors.lean:161`, not in the declaration index) computes the factorisation of a numeral with a `FactorsHelper` certificate: a sorted list of primes whose product is n. This is trial division; Pollard rho, quadratic sieves and other subexponential methods are absent.

targets.target: Polynomial factorisation over finite fields: squarefree decomposition, distinct- and equal-degree factorisation, Cantor–Zassenhaus and Berlekamp with operation counts
targets.note: Only ingredients: an irreducible f over a finite field has deg f ∣ n iff f ∣ X^{qⁿ} − X (the basis of distinct-degree factorisation), the factor count of cyclotomic polynomials over finite fields, and Tau Ceti's multiset of factor degrees modulo p. No factorisation algorithm or operation count exists.

targets.target: Irreducibility proofs and certificates for polynomials
targets.note: Eisenstein's criterion, the degree ≤ 3 root test, Tau Ceti's characterisation of irreducibility by factor degrees and worked mod-p examples exist; no general irreducibility certificate (Rabin or Ben-Or tests, Hensel/Zassenhaus over ℤ) exists.

duplicates.note: Finite-field polynomial factorisation with checked factor products, irreducibility witnesses and separately stated bit-operation and randomness models, the polynomial half of CN.1.

Owns `factorDegrees f p`, the multiset of degrees of the monic irreducible factors of f mod p, with the criterion `factorDegrees f p = {n}` iff `f mod p` is irreducible of degree n, the multiplicity-one lemma at good primes and worked mod-p examples: the mod-p irreducibility-certificate half of CN.1's polynomial targets, and the owner of the Tau Ceti declarations cited for them.

targets.target: Certified integral bases, orders and discriminants
targets.note: Mathlib proves an integral basis exists; Tau Ceti reads the discriminant off a given integral basis, proves disc(minpoly θ) = index² · d_K and the squarefree-mod-p case of Dedekind's criterion, and characterises monogenicity by index one. There is no Round 2 or p-maximal-order algorithm and no general certificate that a proposed basis is integral.

targets.target: Certified decomposition of primes
targets.note: Kummer–Dedekind is proved: for p not dividing the conductor exponent of θ, primes above p correspond to monic irreducible factors of minpoly θ mod p, with residue degrees and ramification indices (Tau Ceti: over a general integrally closed base). Primes dividing the index, which need p-maximal orders, are not covered.

targets.target: Unit groups with an index bound or certificate that proposed units generate
targets.note: Dirichlet's unit theorem, the regulator and the index formula regOfFamily(u)/regulator = [units : ⟨u⟩·torsion] are in Mathlib, with worked cases (units of ℚ(ζ₃), fundamental solutions of Pell equations). No certificate procedure for a given field's fundamental units exists.

targets.target: Class groups with completeness certificates
targets.note: The Minkowski bound (Mathlib) and worked class numbers h(ℚ(√−5)) = 2 and h(ℚ(√−21)) = 4 with an effective class-number bound (Tau Ceti), plus class number one for ℚ(ζ₃) and ℚ(ζ₅), exist. No general class-group computation or completeness certificate exists.

targets.target: Local expansions (p-adic expansions of algebraic numbers, Newton polygons)
targets.note: Hensel's lemma over ℤ_p and p-adic truncations exist; Newton polygons and certified local expansions are absent.

targets.target: Conditional running-time assumptions and independent stopping certificates
targets.note: Nothing in either library.

duplicates.note: Owns the index, the index-discriminant formula, relative Dedekind–Kummer and Dedekind's criterion, the certified integral-basis and prime-decomposition content of CN.2.
Certifies integral bases of quadratic fields and explicit fundamental units at rank one with a proof-carrying elimination certificate, CN.2's unit-group certificate.
Classifies which number-field invariants (class number, regulator, units, prime factorisations) are certified in general or only in worked examples.

targets.target: Exact modular symbols
targets.note: No modular symbols, Manin symbols or Eichler–Shimura period maps in either library.

targets.target: Hecke matrices
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Hecke operators T_n on M_k(Γ₁(N)) and the coefficient recurrence a_m(T_p f) = a_{pm} + χ(p)p^{k−1}a_{m/p}; matrices of Hecke operators on explicit bases are not computed.

targets.target: Exact q-expansions
targets.note: q-expansions exist as power series with exact coefficient formulas for Eisenstein series; no exact computation of q-expansions of general forms.

targets.target: Point counts on elliptic curves over finite fields
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines the point count and trace of Frobenius and proves deg(1 − π) = #E(𝔽_q); Mathlib has the local L-factor. The Hasse bound itself and point-counting algorithms (Schoof) are absent.

targets.target: Isogenies computed through the existing owners
targets.note: Isogenies with degree and kernel exist in Tau Ceti; Vélu's formulas and isogeny computation are absent.

targets.target: Descent computations
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the 2-Selmer group, the rank bound from any finite group containing the descent image, Mordell–Weil and Nagell–Lutz; its own docstring records that no finiteness or effective computation is done.

targets.target: Sturm-style truncation bounds before declaring modular forms equal
targets.note: Mathlib proves the level-one Sturm bound; Tau Ceti proves it for subgroups of finite relative index in SL₂(ℤ) with discrete strict periods (including all Γ₁(N)), in the form 'forms whose q-expansions at ∞ agree up to k·[SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]/12 are equal'.

duplicates.note: Owns the modular-symbol module, Manin symbols and the Hecke action on symbols, the entry point it names for downstream computation.
Constructs modular symbols with Manin symbols, boundary maps and Hecke actions at general level.
Point counts with the Frobenius trace convention and the Hasse bound over finite fields.
Isogeny graphs and certified class-polynomial computations with coefficient and precision certificates.
Turns isogeny and Selmer constructions into finite descent algorithms with certified rank bounds and saturation.

Owns the Sturm bound at general level (`sturm_bound_finiteIndex`, consuming Mathlib's level-one bound) together with finite-dimensionality, which is exactly CN.3's Sturm-style truncation target and the source of the Tau Ceti declarations cited for it.

Also asks for certified point-counting algorithms with the trace convention and a provable error bound, the point-count half of CN.3; the batch already records FF.3 as CN.1's polynomial-factorisation duplicate.

targets.target: Interval or ball arithmetic with precision propagation
targets.note: Mathlib has exact interval arithmetic on ordered structures (its docstring says it is not yet integrated) and certified rational enclosures of π, e and log 2 from Taylor-remainder certificates. Ball arithmetic, floating-point enclosures and precision propagation are absent.

targets.target: Certified roots (root isolation)
targets.note: Descartes' rule of signs and the intermediate value theorem exist; Sturm sequences and certified root isolation are absent.

targets.target: Certified approximations of L-values, and analytic continuation where required
targets.note: Only exact special values (ζ(2), ζ at negative integers) and abstract continuation exist; no numerical L-value enclosures.

targets.target: Validated p-adic numerics with precision tracking
targets.note: p-adic truncations and Hensel's lemma exist; precision tracking does not.

duplicates.note: Certified interval and ball enclosures for period integrals and convergent L-value expressions with proved error bounds.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow.summary: Towards this roadmap Tau Ceti has gone well beyond its 1 September status page: at this baseline Layer 0 is complete (constant-speed reparametrisation, lower semicontinuity, corner smoothing, the piecewise-C¹ comparison, restriction, finiteness and the metric space), and Layer 1 has the geodesic spray with its chart independence and smoothness, local existence and uniqueness of geodesics, constant speed, the maximal interval J(p,v) with its scaling law, the finite-endpoint extension criterion and the manifold inverse function theorem. The pinned Mathlib already provides `CovariantDerivative.IsMetricCompatible` and the Levi-Civita connection with existence and uniqueness, so no local shim is needed; Tau Ceti supplies its smoothness, and the metric length- and geodesic-space API of Layer 4 exists. Genuinely missing: smooth dependence and the geodesic flow on TM, a chosen maximal geodesic, the exponential map and its derivative at 0, all of Layer 2 (normal neighbourhoods, Gauss lemma, minimisation, first variation), the Hopf–Rinow implications apart from Mathlib's `complete_of_proper`, compact ⇒ complete, Riemannian manifolds as length/geodesic spaces, and Riemannian isometries.

targets.target: C¹ length algebra consumed from Mathlib: additivity of `Manifold.pathELength` under subdivision and invariance under differentiable monotone reparametrisation
targets.note: Both lemmas are in Mathlib's `PathELength.lean` (additivity needs no regularity; the reparametrisation lemma needs a monotone differentiable change of parameter and a differentiable curve), and Tau Ceti's piecewise and comparison files consume them rather than re-proving them.

targets.target: Constant-speed reparametrisation of a regular C¹ curve (speed nowhere zero)
targets.note: For γ C¹ on an open set containing [a,b] with nonzero velocity there, Tau Ceti gives a strictly increasing C¹ inverse of accumulated length such that γ ∘ ψ has unit speed, the same endpoints and the same `pathELength`; other constant speeds follow by affine rescaling.

targets.target: Lower semicontinuity of length for C¹ curves converging uniformly on a fixed compact interval to a C¹ limit
targets.note: Exactly the stated form, for eventually C¹ curves with a C¹ limit on `Icc a b`, on a manifold whose extended metric is the Riemannian one (`IsRiemannianManifold`); the proof goes through `pathELength = eVariationOn` for C¹ curves.

targets.target: Piecewise-C¹ paths by finite partitions, length as a sum over pieces, independence under refinement, corner smoothing, and equality of the piecewise infimum with `Manifold.riemannianEDist`
targets.note: All four milestones are proved: partition sums, refinement invariance, the corner-smoothing theorem (a C¹ path on [0,1] with the same endpoints and length) and do Carmo's piecewise infimum equal to Mathlib's C¹ `riemannianEDist`.

targets.target: Restriction of the Riemannian bundle to an open submanifold with its smoothness instance, and Riemannian distance equal to the norm distance on a convex open subset of an inner-product space
targets.note: The restricted metric keeps its regularity (the instances are scoped to `TauCeti`), and for a convex open U of any real inner-product space (finite dimension is not needed) the Riemannian distance of U is ‖x − y‖ₑ.

targets.target: Finiteness of `riemannianEDist` on a connected manifold, then a compatible ordinary metric-space structure consuming `IsRiemannianManifold`
targets.note: Proved on a preconnected manifold (`[PreconnectedSpace M]`, `IsManifold I 1`, continuous Riemannian bundle); the metric space keeps the manifold topology and carries the `IsRiemannianManifold` instance, building on Mathlib's extended-metric construction.

targets.target: Metric compatibility (`CovariantDerivative.IsMetricCompatible`) and existence and uniqueness of the torsion-free metric-compatible (Levi-Civita) connection, reusing `torsion_eq_zero_iff`
targets.note: The pinned Mathlib already contains `IsMetricCompatible`, the Koszul-formula construction of `leviCivitaConnection` (metric and torsion-free) and uniqueness on differentiable vector fields, for a C² manifold with a C¹ Riemannian metric in finite dimension. No local shim is needed; Tau Ceti already consumes these and adds the Koszul characterisation `isLeviCivitaConnection_iff`.

targets.target: Regularity: `ContMDiffCovariantDerivative ∇ ∞` for the Levi-Civita connection, and C^∞ chart Christoffel maps (into bilinear maps) and scalar Christoffel symbols
targets.note: A C^∞ metric on a C^∞ manifold gives a C^∞ connection, and the Christoffel map and symbols are C^n on the base set of each tangent-bundle trivialisation (for a C^(n+2) manifold and C^(n+1) metric). Mathlib's own Levi-Civita file still lists smoothness as future work.

targets.target: Covariant derivative along a curve: linearity, Leibniz rule, locality, reparametrisation, agreement with the ambient derivative on pulled-back fields, chart formula, and covariant acceleration
targets.note: All listed properties are proved (locality through `alongCurveWithin_inter` and `alongCurveWithin_congr`). Covariant acceleration has no separate name: the along-curve derivative of the velocity is used directly, with its chart form in `alongCurveWithin_curveVelocityWithin_eq_zero_iff`.

targets.target: The geodesic predicate `IsGeodesicCurveOn γ s` on parameter sets with unique derivatives, its equivalence with the chart geodesic ODE, and the initial-data predicate
targets.note: As specified: C² on s, unique differentiability, vanishing along-curve derivative of the within-set velocity, equivalence with u'' + Γ(u',u') = 0 in the chart at the current point, and a bundled initial-data predicate.

targets.target: The geodesic spray on TM: chart formula (x,v) ↦ (v, −Γ_x(v,v)), independence of the chart, C^∞ regularity, and integral curves equal to velocity lifts of geodesics (set-restricted)
targets.note: All proved at this baseline, although the roadmap's status page (1 September) listed the spray as having only the Christoffel transformation law.

targets.target: Local existence of the geodesic with initial data (p,v) on an open interval around 0, and uniqueness on the overlap of two such intervals
targets.note: Obtained from Mathlib's integral-curve existence applied to the spray, on a boundaryless finite-dimensional C^∞ manifold with C^∞ metric; uniqueness assumes the tangent bundle is Hausdorff.

targets.target: C^∞ dependence on time and initial data and the local geodesic flow on TM
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves a C^(n+1) local flow for a C^(n+1) vector field on a finite-dimensional normed space. Smooth local flows on manifolds, and the geodesic flow on TM, are absent.

targets.target: Constant speed of geodesics on preconnected parameter sets
targets.note: For any preconnected parameter set (with the predicate's unique-differentiability condition) the norm of the within-set velocity is constant; the componentwise form for disconnected sets is not stated separately.

targets.target: The maximal open interval J(p,v) from genuine geodesic witnesses, and homogeneity γ_{p,λv}(t) = γ_{p,v}(λt) with the precise relation between the domains
targets.note: J(p,v) is defined as the union of open witness intervals, shown open, order-connected and containing 0, and t ∈ J(p,a•v) ↔ a·t ∈ J(p,v) for a ≠ 0; affine rescaling of witnesses is proved. There is no chosen maximal geodesic γ_{p,v} on J(p,v), so the homogeneity identity itself is not stated.

targets.target: Finite-endpoint extension criterion for integral curves on maximal intervals, at both endpoints
targets.note: Proved for any C¹ vector field on a boundaryless Hausdorff manifold modelled on a complete space (cluster-point and sequential forms, left and right), with the escape lemma and a maximal integral curve.

targets.target: Exponential map: expDomain p, exp_p v = γ_{p,v}(1), 0 ∈ expDomain p, exp_p 0 = p, openness, smoothness via the time-one flow, t ∈ J(p,v) ↔ t•v ∈ expDomain p, star-shapedness
targets.note: No Riemannian exponential map in either library; only the domain facts about `geodesicInterval` above exist.

targets.target: The derivative of exp_p at 0 is the identity under `NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace`, with the strict-derivative form
targets.note: Only the tangent-space identification exists.

targets.target: Manifold inverse function theorem: a C¹ map whose mfderiv is a continuous linear equivalence is a local diffeomorphism
targets.note: In `TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/LocalDiffeomorph.lean` as the roadmap asks, for 𝕂 = ℝ or ℂ, C^n (1 ≤ n) on an open set around an interior point of a manifold modelled on a complete space, so boundaryless manifolds are a special case. Its application to exp_p is absent with exp_p.

targets.target: Pointwise geodesic completeness (d_p) and the equivalence (a_p) ↔ (d_p)
targets.note: Absent; depends on the exponential map.

duplicates.note: Builds an exponential map from integral curves, proves its derivative at 0 is the identity and deduces a local diffeomorphism at 0 from the manifold inverse function theorem, the same pattern and the same shared theorem as Layer 1's exp_p milestones.

targets.target: Normal neighbourhoods and normal coordinates, and the local logarithm log_p with smoothness, log_p p = 0 and the two inverse identities
targets.note: Absent; the inverse function theorem that would produce it exists, but there is no exponential map.

targets.target: The Gauss lemma and its polar length inequality on a normal ball
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Radial segments minimise length among piecewise-C¹ competitors inside the normal ball, with the two equality statements (affine radial geodesic; minimisers up to monotone reparametrisation)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Escape estimate and the local distance identity pathELength I γ 0 1 = edist p (γ 1) for radial segments in a smaller ball
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: First variation of energy: energy of C¹ curves, fixed-endpoint variations and variation fields, integration by parts, criticality exactly for geodesics
targets.note: Absent; the energy and variation hits in Tau Ceti concern PDE and J-holomorphic curves.

targets.target: The TFAE of (a_p), (b), (c), global (d) and (e_p), with (a_p) ⇒ (f_p), and (e_p) in the stated exhaustion form
targets.note: No Hopf–Rinow statement in either library.

targets.target: (c) ⇒ (d): metric completeness extends maximal geodesics past finite endpoints, via Cauchy base curves, bounded velocities in a trivialisation, a convergent subsequence in TM and the extension criterion
targets.note: The extension criterion and constant speed are available; the implication itself is absent.
Absent; needs the exponential map.

targets.target: (a_p) ⇒ (f_p): every q is joined to p by a geodesic on [0,1] realising `edist p q`, with distance-realising subsegments
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: (a_p) and (f_p) ⇒ (b): closed balls are images of closed tangent balls under exp_p, hence compact, so M is proper
targets.note: Only the generic properness criteria exist.

targets.target: (b) ⇒ (c) by the instance `complete_of_proper`
targets.note: Mathlib's instance (proper metric spaces are complete); it is missing from the declaration index but present at the cited line.

targets.target: (b) ⇔ (e_p): exhaustion by compact sets with divergent distance from p
targets.note: The equivalence is not stated; closed balls exhausting the space and properness exist.

targets.target: Base-point propagation: (a_p) at one point gives global (d), hence (a_q) and (d_q) for every q
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Compact ⇒ geodesically complete, by the connected route through `proper_of_compact`, `complete_of_proper` and (c) ⇒ (d)
targets.note: The consumed instances exist, and Tau Ceti proves a C¹ vector field on a compact boundaryless manifold is complete (not applicable to the spray on the noncompact TM). The corollary is absent because (c) ⇒ (d) is.

targets.target: Metric length-space API in `TauCeti/Topology/MetricSpace/Length.lean`: curve length as the supremum of sums of successive distances, and length spaces
targets.note: Curve length is Mathlib's `eVariationOn`, and `IsLengthSpace` says the extended distance is the infimum of lengths of continuous curves on [0,1] joining the points, in the file the roadmap names.

targets.target: Metric geodesic-space API: constant-speed segments with dist(γ s, γ t) = |s − t|·dist x y, geodesic spaces, and geodesic spaces are length spaces
targets.note: Exactly as specified, with real normed spaces as geodesic spaces.

targets.target: A complete connected Riemannian manifold is a length space and a geodesic space
targets.note: Absent. The length-space half is close: C¹ path length equals total variation, and short C¹ paths exist below any bound above the distance. The geodesic-space half needs (f_p).

targets.target: Smooth Riemannian isometries: transport of the Levi-Civita connection, preservation of geodesics, maximal intervals, exponential maps and geodesic completeness, through `IsRiemannianManifold`
targets.note: No Riemannian isometry notion in either library; the only hits are linear isometries of the round sphere with no metric.

review.notes: Checked all 194 targets of the 33 layers, 375 distinct declaration citations and 89 duplicate claims. Every citation resolves at the stated library, file and line (four are absent from declarations.tsv but present in the source exactly as cited: `PMF` at Mathlib/Probability/ProbabilityMassFunction/Basic.lean:46, whose universe annotation `PMF.{u}` the index misses, and the instances `proper_of_compact` and `complete_of_proper` at Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/ProperSpace.lean:93 and :104 - the audit already flags the last one). No citation is private, an axiom or a bare structure field, and no cited file contains a `sorry` in a proof; the nine Tau Ceti and 44 Mathlib files whose text contains the word are all docstrings, and none of them is cited. Every verdict agrees with its targets under the rule that `built` means no absent or partial target, `not built` means none present, and `partly built` means at least one of each; no layer needed a verdict change. The one `built` layer (HopfRinow Layer 0) was confirmed target by target against the Lean sources, and the three `process` layers (HC.6, HR.7, CN.5) are export, acceptance-test and reproducibility bookkeeping as their descriptions say. I re-searched independently, by concept and by Mathlib naming convention, in declarations.tsv and in both whole source trees, every absent or partial claim whose concept has a standard name, and about two thirds of the rest: no Riemannian exponential map, Gauss lemma, normal neighbourhood, first variation of energy, Hopf-Rinow statement, Riemannian isometry, geodesic flow or chosen maximal geodesic; no Cohen-Macaulay, Auslander-Buchsbaum, complete-intersection, catenary or excellent-ring predicate, no depth invariant (only Rees' theorem in Mathlib/RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean), no perfect complex, Tor-amplitude, derived completion, derived Nakayama, lim-1, completed tensor product, Schlessinger criterion, deformation functor, hull or ultraproduct of varying rings; no Habiro ring, cyclotomic completion, Lambda-ring, Adams operation, delta-ring, q-Witt or big Witt ring, and q-Pochhammer symbols are still a Mathlib TODO; no Hermite normal form, LLL, Miller-Rabin, AKS, Pollard rho, Cantor-Zassenhaus, Berlekamp, Velu, Schoof, modular symbol, Newton polygon, Sturm sequence, ball arithmetic or Hasse bound. Two files the audit does not cite, TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/MetricVariation.lean and MetricBridge.lean, are further Layer-0 support (metric variation equals path length on an open submanifold, and the chart-displacement estimate), not the first variation of energy, so Layer 2 stays absent. All 89 duplicate claims point at live atlas layers - none retired - and reading the target descriptions confirms each overlap; the low-scoring ones are same-roadmap cross-references and are correct, including that the atlas gives HR.5-number-field-comparison the whole of HR.5's description. Candidates I checked and rejected as duplicates because they are declared consumers of the batch's own roadmaps: OptimalTransport Layers 7 and 8 and GeometricTopology Layer 7 (they consume HopfRinow's connection, exponential map and length-space API), GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1 and AutomorphicCongruences L3 (both list DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra as a dependency), LanglandsParameterStacks LP4 and EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.1. The audit's own factual asides hold: CN.2 does still list the retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4 as an input, Mathlib's `Polynomial.normalizedFactors_cyclotomic_card` does give Phi_5 four factors over F_11, and `CommRingCat.equalizerForkIsLimit` does supply HR.7's Suggested.lean universal property.
